R-ops-2 (A dropped webhook is only logged at debug level, as free text) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.recommendation: Wait between attempts with an exponential backoff and jitter (for example 1 s, 2 s, 4 s, 8 s, capped), and do not retry responses that will not change on a retry (4xx other than 408/429). Scenario: a merchant endpoint returns 503 during a 10-second restart; each non-ok response loops straight into the next attempt, so all five POSTs are spent within the outage and the event is dropped, while a merchant under load receives five requests in a burst. The retries are bounded and deduplicated by `x-event-id`, but the step's criterion requires them to be spaced.
findings.title: Webhook retries fire back-to-back with no backoff

findings.recommendation: Log the final drop at error (and each failed attempt at warn) through the service's structured logger, with fields such as `eventId`, `paymentId`, merchant id, `attempt`, the HTTP status or error, and the outcome, and count drops in a metric an alert can watch. Scenario: a merchant's endpoint is down for an hour; every settlement notification is permanently lost, but the only trace is a `console.debug` line, which production log levels usually discard, so neither the operator nor the merchant learns the payment was never notified. Non-ok responses (lines 17-19) leave no trace at all: the status code a merchant returned is never logged, so even with debug on an operator cannot tell a 500 from a 404. `deliver` returns `false` but the caller at line 34 ignores it, so the drop is silent end to end.
findings.title: A dropped webhook is only logged at debug level, as free text
